content:
For years, collectors have been vying to acquire memorabilia from Steve Jobs, and a new item is bound to generate immense interest: his eighth-grade science fair project, featuring two demonstration circuits and a warning note he gave to his teacher.

This piece has been kept at the Jobs family property in Los Altos, and is now one of over 200 lots in an auction celebrating Apple's 50th anniversary...

To mark its 50th year, Apple has partnered with RR Auctions to host a two-part auction titled "Steve Jobs and the Computer Revolution: Celebrating 50 Years of Apple." The first part has already sold the company's first-ever check for an eye-watering $2.4 million.

The second part of the auction features this science fair project.

The warning note likely alerted his teacher that the circuits might burn out if left running too long. At the time of writing, the online bid is still under $3,000, but that's sure to change.

There's also a still-working early Apple 1 computer.

And an original iPod development prototype.
